source.title: How Matryoshka Sparse AutoEncoders Recover Feature Hierarchies That Vanilla SAEs Lose

record.file_problem: The full post is present, but some equations are missing or do not render; the post also notes this.
record.tranche_reason: It compares vanilla and Matryoshka SAE training on hierarchical synthetic features and reports feature recovery, a different method and measure from a dictionary-size sweep.
record.gate_note: The toy-model clean-feature recovery results bear on feature splitting and the effect of the training objective. The TinyStories FVU, L0, and dead-feature results do not measure feature hierarchy or splitting, so they are not rows. The post's general descriptions of prior work are not treated as its own results.
record.test_reason: It reruns the Matryoshka paper's hierarchical toy model, comparing vanilla and Matryoshka objectives on clean-feature recovery. This bears on whether the objective drives splitting and mangling of hierarchical features (V6). It does not sweep dictionary size.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that Matryoshka SAEs avoid absorption in the toy model, recovering 20/20 features versus 11/20 for vanilla. They also say the tradeoff 'holds at scale': on TinyStories, Matryoshka pays a small FVU penalty (≈0.013) at matched L0. They link that penalty to the paper's claim of feature-structure gains but do not measure feature structure there.
record.recipe_differences: The post compares vanilla SAE training with nested-prefix Matryoshka training on a hierarchical toy model; it does not perform the claim's dictionary-size sweep or measure split-feature directions and input coverage.
record.problems: The feature-recovery evidence is limited to a controlled toy model. The TinyStories results report reconstruction and sparsity metrics rather than feature structure, and no uncertainty estimates are given.
record.rows_left_out: TinyStories results in Replication Results are left out because FVU, L0, and dead-feature percentages do not measure splitting or hierarchy. Toy-model FVU and L0 are likewise not feature-structure measures.

untested.parts: No dictionary-size sweep, input-coverage test or direction comparison.
TinyStories run reports only FVU, L0 and dead features; no splitting measure at scale or in open releases.

Parent non-firing where a child fires is not measured separately; the effect of size or sparsity changes is not tested. 'Absorbs' is the author's description of the vanilla failures, not a measured quantity.
No cross-size decomposition or novel-latent analysis.
Only one alternative objective (Matryoshka), one toy distribution and one seed; no feature-structure result on a real model.

record.verdict_notes: This is a blog replication of the Matryoshka SAE paper, which is not an original source here. In the toy model, vanilla reconstructs better (FVU 0.000 vs 0.021), so Matryoshka costs some reconstruction. No uncertainty or seeds are reported. Some equations do not render, but the results tables are readable.

versions.untested_parts: No increasing dictionary-size sweep, feature-input partition test, or comparison of directions is reported.
The TinyStories run does not report feature-splitting or hierarchy measurements, and the study does not test large models or open SAE releases for this pattern.
No nested feature-family or geometric-proximity measurement is reported.
The study does not measure parent firing where child features take over, or test whether changing SAE size or sparsity fixes that behavior.
No cross-size decomposition of larger-SAE latents into smaller-SAE latents, or measurement of novel latents, is reported.
The objective comparison is on a controlled hierarchical toy model; the TinyStories results do not measure feature structure. Other objectives and whether the result generalizes are not tested.

relation.reason: Its own toy results bear on V6.

tranche.reason: It reruns the Matryoshka paper's toy to compare a different objective on the same question. Because it is a replication, T1 is arguable, but T2 is acceptable.

source_check.notes: The post says the 9 mangled vanilla features are the parent/child ones, absorbed and split, but does not measure this. 'Clean' means best cosine per true feature, with no threshold given. Achieved L0 differs (Matryoshka 1.13, vanilla 0.86) against a 1.2338 target. Matryoshka's FVU is higher in the toy too (0.021 vs 0.000), despite the post's earlier claim of better reconstruction. The TinyStories section gives only FVU, L0 and dead features (dFVU about 0.013), so it bears on no version.

statements.problem: The numbers for this study match the text: 20 features, 20 latents, target L0 1.2338, 11/20 vs 20/20. The text gives no run or seed count but reports one result per method, so 'single run' / 'one seed' is a fair reading. The group condition 'matched L0' holds only for the target; achieved L0 was 1.13 (Matryoshka) vs 0.86 (vanilla).
The text gives 20/20 clean features for Matryoshka (r2). The statement already says this study reports a single run.
